mainTopic: End of the broken-barrel-of-תרומה dispute, the הדרן of the first chapter, and the opening משנה of כל שעה on benefit from חמץ
overview: This amud finishes the first chapter of פסחים and begins the second. First, the גמרא rules that the compromise of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי cannot decide the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about impure תרומה wine: pour it out, or use it for sprinkling. Then it returns to the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about a broken barrel of תרומה wine above impure חולין. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא limits their dispute to a case where there is less than one hundred times as much חולין below. With one hundred, everyone agrees not to make the תרומה impure by hand. A ברייתא supports this. רבא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע give two ways to explain its puzzling wording. After the הדרן, a new משנה teaches that as long as one may eat חמץ, one may also feed it to animals, sell it to a גוי, and benefit from it. After that time, all benefit is forbidden. It also records the dispute between רבי יהודה and חכמים on how to destroy חמץ. The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording fits neither רבי יהודה nor רבי מאיר, and רבה בר עולא explains it according to רבן גמליאל. The amud ends by explaining why the משנה lists both בהמה and חיה, why it adds עופות, and why it needs to say one may sell to a גוי: to reject בית שמאי in favor of בית הלל.

steps.title: A third opinion does not settle the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects treating the compromise of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי as a deciding vote between בית שמאי and בית הלל about impure תרומה wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The decision of a third opinion is not considered a decision.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the discussion from the previous amud. בית שמאי say impure תרומה wine is poured out, and בית הלל say it may be used for sprinkling. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי split the case (field or house, or new or old wine), and the חכמים answer that his view cannot settle the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי agrees with each side only in part: in one case he rules like בית שמאי, and in the other like בית הלל. Such a split is a separate, third position, not a tie-breaker. So the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל stays as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: A deciding opinion that settles a dispute between two earlier views
Third, here meaning a third opinion

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a third view is never valuable. It means only that here it cannot serve as the deciding vote, because it argues from a different reason.

phrases.english: The decision of a third opinion does not decide.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the view of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, cited on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the response, begun on the previous amud, to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's compromise about impure תרומה wine.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects using רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's compromise as a tie-breaker between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He agrees with each side only in part, so his view is a third opinion and cannot count as deciding for either one.

steps.title: The dispute applies only when there is less than one hundred below
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא limits the מחלוקת to a case where the תרומה falls into less than one hundred סאה of impure חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The dispute is about a case where the תרומה fell into less than one hundred סאה of impure חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in to define exactly when רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue. They argue only when the impure wine below is less than one hundred times the תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With less than one hundred times as much, the תרומה is not nullified. The whole lower vat becomes a mixture (מדומע) that non-כהנים may not drink. Because it is impure, a כהן may not drink it either, so the owner loses all his חולין. That big loss is why רבי יהושע allows making the תרומה impure by hand to save the חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than one hundred (times the amount)
Ritually impure, non-sacred (ordinary) produce or wine

steps.whyThisMatters: A one-in-one-hundred ratio is the amount needed to nullify תרומה (בטול במאה). So the size of the lower vat decides whether there is any loss at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
The dispute is where it fell
into less than one hundred se'ah
of impure non-sacred wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside the third opinion, the גמרא now narrows the case in which the main dispute applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue only when the lower vat holds less than one hundred times the amount of תרומה.

steps.title: With one hundred below, everyone agrees not to defile it by hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא continues: if there is one hundred times as much below, all agree the תרומה should be left to run down on its own, and no one should make it impure by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it fell into one hundred סאה of impure חולין, everyone agrees: let it go down and become impure by itself, but one should not make it impure with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement. In the one-hundred case, even רבי יהושע agrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one hundred times as much below, the תרומה is nullified in the חולין. The lower wine stays permitted to non-כהנים, so the owner loses nothing. Since there is no loss to prevent, there is no reason to actively make holy תרומה impure. All that is left is to let it fall on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it go down and become impure by itself
He should not make it impure with his own hand

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהושע changed his opinion. His leniency in the משנה was only to prevent the loss of the חולין. Here there is no loss, so his reason does not apply.

phrases.english: But if it fell into one hundred of impure non-sacred wine —
all agree: let it go down and become impure,
and he should not make it impure by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל נָפְלָה לְמֵאָה חוּלִּין טְמֵאִין דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement by giving the case where there is no dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there is one hundred times as much below, everyone agrees: let the תרומה become impure on its own, but do not make it impure by hand.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the one-hundred limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states the same rule. With one hundred below, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree: save a רביעית in purity if you can, and if not, let it go down without defiling it by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: If a barrel broke in the upper winepress, and below it are one hundred measures of impure חולין, רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי יהושע. If one can save a רביעית of it in purity, he should save it. If not, let it go down and become impure, but he should not make it impure by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא describes the exact one-hundred case and shows the two תנאים agreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement point for point. It names the one-hundred case, says the two sides agree, and gives the same ruling: do not make it impure by hand. That confirms that the משנה's dispute is limited to less than one hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
A quarter-לוג, a small liquid measure

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is only when there is less than one hundred below, where the חולין would be lost. With one hundred, the תרומה is nullified. Then everyone agrees: save a רביעית in purity if possible, and otherwise let it fall, but never make it impure by hand.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
A barrel that broke in the upper winepress,
and below it are one hundred of impure non-sacred wine —
Rabbi Eliezer agrees with Rabbi Yehoshua
that if he is able to save from it
a quarter-log in purity — he should save it,
and if not — let it go down and become impure
and he should not make it impure by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This supports the statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא in steps 2 and 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's claim that in the one-hundred case everyone agrees not to make the תרומה impure by hand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly describes the one-hundred case and states that the two תנאים agree.

steps.title: The names in the ברייתא seem to be backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording 'רבי אליעזר concedes to רבי יהושע', since the agreed rule actually matches רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This phrase, 'רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי יהושע', is strange. It should have said 'רבי יהושע agrees with רבי אליעזר'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the ברייתא it just brought as proof and points out that its wording seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the original מחלוקת, רבי אליעזר is the one who says never to make the תרומה impure by hand, while רבי יהושע allows it. The agreed rule in the ברייתא (do not make it impure by hand) is רבי אליעזר's position. So it is רבי יהושע who is giving in, and the ברייתא should say 'רבי יהושע concedes to רבי אליעזר'.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees / concedes (one side gives in to the other's view)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Concedes to' means the first person is giving in to the second person's view. So the person named first is the one who moved. That is why the order of names matters here.

phrases.english: This phrase, "Rabbi Eliezer concedes to Rabbi Yehoshua" —
"Rabbi Yehoshua concedes to Rabbi Eliezer"
is what it should have said!
phrases.notes: The agreed rule matches רבי אליעזר's position, so רבי יהושע is the one conceding.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא brought as proof in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'מודה רבי אליעזר לרבי יהושע' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The shared ruling (do not defile by hand) is רבי אליעזר's own view, so רבי יהושע is the one conceding, and the names appear reversed.

steps.title: רבא says to switch the names
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers simply: reverse the names in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Switch the names.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the question and fixes the ברייתא by flipping the names, so it reads 'רבי יהושע concedes to רבי אליעזר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a text correction. רבא agrees the wording as we have it does not fit the law, so he changes the text to match the logic. The law itself does not change.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse / switch (the names or the opinions)

phrases.english: Rava said: Reverse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5 by changing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's wording is correct as written
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read 'רבי יהושע concedes to רבי אליעזר'

steps.title: Keep the names: the case is a vessel that is pure inside and impure outside
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע keeps the original wording. The ברייתא is teaching that רבי אליעזר agrees one may save the wine even with a vessel whose outside is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Really, do not switch the names. Here we are dealing with a vessel whose inside is pure and whose outside is impure. You might think we should make a rabbinic decree not to use it, in case its outside touches the תרומה. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: the wording is fine, because the 'concession' is about a different point than we thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concession is not about defiling by hand. It is about saving a רביעית in purity when the only vessel available is pure inside but impure outside. One might think רבי אליעזר, who is so careful about the תרומה's purity, would forbid this out of fear the impure outside will touch the wine. The ברייתא teaches that he agrees with רבי יהושע that it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (redefines the case)
Its inside is pure and its outside is impure
Let us make a rabbinic decree
You might have thought ... so it teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers: רבא changes the text. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע keeps the text and explains that the concession is about using a vessel with an impure outside to save the wine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא choice: either fix the text (איפוך) or keep the text and redefine the case (הכא במאי עסקינן).

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Actually, do not reverse it.
With what case are we dealing here?
With a vessel whose inside is pure and whose outside is impure.
phrases.notes: The outside became impure only by rabbinic law, through impure liquids.

phrases.english: You might have said: let us make a decree
in case its outside touches the terumah.
So it teaches us that we do not.
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר agrees with רבי יהושע that one may save the רביעית with such a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to Step 5's question, rejecting the need for רבא's text change.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) so the original wording fits
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would decree against saving the wine with a vessel whose outside is impure, in case it touches the תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: No decree: רבי אליעזר concedes to רבי יהושע that one may save a רביעית even with such a vessel

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter אור לארבעה עשר
steps.stepSummary: The first chapter of פסחים, אור לארבעה עשר, ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter אור לארבעה עשר.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line marking the end of the first chapter of פסחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No legal argument here. It shows that the discussion of searching for חמץ and the related purity topics is done, and a new chapter is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (formula for finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, "On the night of the fourteenth"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that contained Steps 1-7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of פסחים is complete.

steps.title: While חמץ may be eaten, all benefit is allowed; after its time, all benefit is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that as long as eating חמץ is allowed, one may feed it to animals, sell it to a non-Jew, and benefit from it. After its time, benefit is forbidden, even using it as fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as one is allowed to eat חמץ, one may feed it to domestic animals, wild animals, and birds, sell it to a non-Jew, and benefit from it. Once its time has passed, benefit from it is forbidden, and one may not even use it to heat an oven or stove.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter (כל שעה) opens with a משנה that links the time you may eat חמץ to the time you may benefit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets the rule: permission to benefit lasts as long as permission to eat. After the deadline, the חמץ becomes אסור בהנאה, forbidden for any use. Even burning it for heat is forbidden, because you would gain from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to benefit from it
Forbidden to benefit from (no use at all, not only eating)

steps.confusionAlert: Forbidden 'to benefit from' is stricter than forbidden 'to eat'. It means no use at all: no selling, no feeding animals, not even using it as fuel.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The entire time that it is permitted to eat (chametz),
one may feed it to domestic animals, wild animals, and birds,
and sell it to a gentile, and benefit from it is permitted.
Once its time has passed, benefit from it is forbidden,
and one may not heat an oven or stove with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן of Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Benefit from חמץ is allowed as long as eating it is allowed; after its time all benefit is forbidden, even as fuel.

steps.title: How to destroy חמץ: only burning, or other ways too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says חמץ must be destroyed only by burning. חכמים say it may also be crumbled and scattered in the wind or thrown into the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Getting rid of חמץ can only be done by burning it. חכמים say: One may also crumble it and scatter it in the wind, or throw it into the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about the required method of ביעור חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds there is one required method: burning. חכמים say the goal is simply to destroy the חמץ, so any method that fully gets rid of it works, such as scattering crumbs or throwing it into the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: Crumbles it and scatters it in the wind

steps.whatToRemember: The new משנה teaches two things: (1) benefit from חמץ follows the time for eating it, and after that all benefit is forbidden; (2) רבי יהודה requires burning, while חכמים allow any method that destroys it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The common custom of burning חמץ on ערב פסח connects to this מחלוקת about the method of ביעור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The removal of chametz is only by burning.
And the Sages say:
One may also crumble it and scatter it to the wind
or throw it into the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין בִּיעוּר חָמֵץ אֶלָּא שְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from benefit from חמץ to the method of destroying it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: ביעור חמץ only by burning. חכמים: crumbling and scattering in the wind, or throwing into the sea, also works.

steps.title: Inference from the opening words of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. If you may feed animals while eating is permitted, then once eating is forbidden, you may not feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: "Whenever it is permitted to eat, one may feed." This implies that whenever it is not permitted to eat, one may not feed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by drawing a simple inference from the משנה's words. This is a setup: the inference will be used right away to ask whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties feeding animals to the time when eating is allowed. The flip side is that feeding stops exactly when eating stops. That claim, that the two times line up perfectly, is what the next step will test.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Opening of the גמרא on the new משנה.

phrases.english: Whenever it is permitted to eat, one may feed,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כׇּל שָׁעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּתָּר לֶאֱכוֹל —
phrases.english: which implies that whenever it is not permitted to eat,
one may not feed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כׇּל שָׁעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּתָּר לֶאֱכוֹל אֵינוֹ מַאֲכִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה presented in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, feeding animals is forbidden once eating חמץ is forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, there is an hour when you may not eat חמץ but may still feed it to animals. That clashes with the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה? Because according to רבי יהודה, there is the fifth hour, when one may not eat but may still feed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference by pointing to רבי יהודה's view. For him, there is a gap hour when eating is forbidden but feeding is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference said feeding ends exactly when eating ends. For רבי יהודה, eating ends after the fourth hour, but benefit, including feeding, continues through the fifth hour. So the משנה seems to exclude רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggested conclusion that is often rejected)

phrases.english: Shall we say our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?
For if it followed Rabbi Yehuda,
there is the fifth hour, when one does not eat,
yet one may feed.
phrases.notes: Benefit is still allowed during the fifth hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the inference of step 11 against רבי יהודה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה can follow רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יהודה, eating and feeding end at different times. That contradicts the משנה's implication that they end together.

steps.title: The source for רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה's hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier משנה. רבי מאיר says you may eat until the end of the fifth hour. רבי יהודה says you may eat only until the end of the fourth hour, then you hold it during the fifth, and you burn at the start of the sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי מאיר says one may eat during the whole fifth hour and burn at the start of the sixth. רבי יהודה says one may eat during the whole fourth hour, hold it in suspension during the whole fifth hour, and burn at the start of the sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves the challenge in step 12. It quotes the משנה earlier in the מסכת that lays out the hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the fifth hour is a "suspended" hour. You may not eat the חמץ, but you also do not burn it yet, so benefit, such as feeding animals, is still allowed. For רבי מאיר, eating and burning have no gap between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it suspended: you don't eat it, but you don't burn it yet
The start of the sixth hour

steps.confusionAlert: תולין does not mean "burn" or "eat." It is the middle hour: no eating, no burning yet, but benefit is still permitted.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Meir says:
one may eat during the entire fifth hour,
and one burns at the beginning of the sixth.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אוֹכְלִין כׇּל אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: one may eat during the entire fourth hour,
one holds it in suspension during the entire fifth,
and one burns at the beginning of the sixth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the challenge in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה has an hour when eating is forbidden but benefit is allowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה earlier in פסחים recording the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The wording does not fit רבי מאיר either
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, it should have said "whenever one eats, he feeds." The phrase "whenever it is permitted to eat" sounds as if it is talking about someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, what? Does it follow רבי מאיר? Then this phrase, "whenever it is permitted to eat, one may feed," should have said, "whenever one eats, he feeds."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה, does it follow רבי מאיר? It then shows that the wording does not fit רבי מאיר well either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the same person eats and feeds until the same moment. The natural wording would then be the simple "whenever one eats, he feeds." The impersonal phrase "it is permitted to eat" hints that the eater and the feeder are two different people.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? (the alternative also has a problem)

phrases.english: But rather, what? It follows Rabbi Meir?
This phrase, "Whenever it is permitted to eat, one may feed,"
"Whenever one eats, he feeds"
it should have said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Considers the other option, רבי מאיר, and shows that it also fails on the wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's view calls for simpler wording. The impersonal phrasing suggests two different people, which does not match his view.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: the משנה follows רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא says the משנה follows רבן גמליאל. He holds that חולין may be eaten through the fourth hour and תרומה through the fifth, with burning at the start of the sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: Our משנה follows רבן גמליאל. As we learned: רבן גמליאל says, חולין may be eaten during the whole fourth hour, תרומה during the whole fifth, and one burns at the start of the sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא resolves the dilemma: the משנה follows neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה but רבן גמליאל. The source for his view is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל splits the timing by the type of food. Ordinary חמץ (חולין) is eaten until the end of the fourth hour. A כהן may still eat חמץ of תרומה until the end of the fifth. This creates two different eaters, which sets up the solution to the wording problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly portion, which only a כהן may eat

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
Our Mishnah follows Rabban Gamliel.
As we learned: Rabban Gamliel says:
Non-sacred food is eaten during the entire fourth hour,
teruma during the entire fifth,
and one burns at the beginning of the sixth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: מַתְנִיתִין רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets out of the dilemma of steps 12 and 14 by assigning the משנה to a third תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribute the משנה to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow either רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה, and neither fits.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבן גמליאל, who distinguishes between חולין and תרומה.

steps.title: How the משנה reads according to רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means: as long as a כהן may still eat תרומה, an ישראל may feed his חולין to his animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it is saying: whenever a כהן is permitted to eat תרומה, an ישראל may feed חולין to domesticated animals, wild animals, and birds.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא explains how to read the משנה's words under רבן גמליאל's view. This solves the wording problem raised in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Permitted to eat" refers to the כהן eating תרומה, which lasts through the fifth hour. "Feeds" refers to the ישראל feeding his own חולין during that same time, even though he himself can no longer eat it. That is exactly why the משנה used impersonal wording: two different people are involved.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it is saying (a reinterpretation)
A regular Jew, not a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The one who is permitted to eat is the כהן, eating תרומה. The one who feeds is the ישראל, feeding חולין. They are not the same person.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה בר עולא, the משנה follows רבן גמליאל. An ישראל may feed his חמץ to animals through the fifth hour, as long as a כהן may still eat תרומה.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שָׁעָה שֶׁמּוּתָּר לֶאֱכוֹל כֹּהֵן בִּתְרוּמָה,
phrases.english: whenever it is permitted for a priest to eat teruma,
an Israelite may feed non-sacred food
to domesticated animals, to wild animals, and to birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה בר עולא's answer by rereading the משנה's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpret the wording: two different people are involved.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eater and the feeder are the same person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eater is a כהן eating תרומה, and the feeder is an ישראל feeding חולין.

steps.title: Why mention both domesticated and wild animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to list both a בהמה and a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to teach domesticated animals, and why do I need it to teach wild animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail of the משנה's wording. It asks why both kinds of animals are listed when one seems to be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding חמץ to an animal seems like the same law no matter which animal it is. The question assumes that listing both is extra wording, and it asks what each one adds.

phrases.english: Why do I need it to teach domesticated animal,
why do I need it to teach wild animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from whose view the משנה follows to why its list of animals is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of בהמה and חיה adds that the other would not teach.

steps.title: Both are needed: the first half of the explanation
steps.stepSummary: Both are needed. If only בהמה were taught, we would say it is allowed because you can see leftovers. A חיה hides its leftovers, so we might say feeding it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If it had taught only domesticated animals, that is because if it leaves some over, he sees it. But a wild animal, if it leaves some over, hides it, so one might say it is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a צריכא, explaining why each case is needed. This passage gives the first half: why בהמה alone would not teach us about חיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a בהמה, leftover חמץ stays in plain view, so the owner will notice it and get rid of it. A חיה hides leftover food, so the owner might later own hidden חמץ without knowing it. Because of that worry, we would have thought feeding a חיה is forbidden near the deadline, so the משנה had to say it explicitly.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: each case teaches something the other does not
I would have said no (it is not allowed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic צריכא pattern. It shows that the משנה lists two similar cases because each one carries its own reason, and the reasons do not automatically transfer. The second half (why חיה alone would not be enough) is given in step 19.

phrases.english: It is necessary.
For had it taught domesticated animal,
that is because if it leaves some over, he sees it.
But a wild animal,
which, if it leaves some over, hides it away,
I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17, starting with why בהמה alone is not enough.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each case has its own reason. A בהמה's leftovers are visible, while a חיה hides its leftovers, so being lenient with one would not prove we should be lenient with the other.

steps.title: Why a wild animal alone would not teach us about a domestic animal
steps.stepSummary: This is the second half of the צריכא. If the משנה had taught only חיה, we might think feeding is allowed because a חיה hides its leftovers. A בהמה leaves food out in the open. The owner may not notice it and could then violate בל יראה and בל ימצא. So we might have thought feeding a בהמה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only a wild animal, we would say it is allowed because, even if it leaves food over, at least it hides it. But a domestic animal sometimes leaves food over and the owner does not think about it, and he ends up violating 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found.' So we might say feeding it is not allowed. Therefore both cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the previous step. It shows that teaching only חיה would not be enough either, so the משנה really needs both animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 showed that בהמה alone would not teach us about חיה. Now the גמרא shows the reverse. A חיה hides its leftovers, so they are out of the way. A בהמה leaves them lying around, and a careless owner could transgress בל יראה. Each animal has its own possible reason to forbid feeding, so the משנה must mention both.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not pay attention to it
The prohibitions of having חמץ seen or found in one's possession on פסח
It is necessary (both cases are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: Each animal has a different risk. A בהמה's leftovers are visible but may be forgotten, while a חיה's leftovers are hidden. That is why the משנה must teach both.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 18 used 'you can see the leftovers' as a reason to permit feeding a בהמה, because he will notice and remove them. Here, the same open leftovers are a reason to worry, because he may not pay attention. Both arguments are part of the צריכא: each one shows what we might have mistakenly thought.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only a wild animal,
[I would say it is allowed] because if it leaves food over,
at least it hides it.
But a domestic animal:
sometimes it leaves food over
and he does not think about it,
and he ends up transgressing
'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found.'
So I might say it is not allowed. Therefore, both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכא begun in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Teaching only חיה would not teach us about בהמה, because a בהמה's open leftovers could lead to violating בל יראה. So both must be listed.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention birds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה also lists עופות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need birds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next word in the משנה, birds. It sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having explained why both בהמה and חיה are needed, the גמרא checks whether עופות add anything new. Birds do not seem to raise a separate problem.

phrases.english: Why do I need birds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question about the משנה's list to its third item.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law is taught by mentioning עופות?

steps.title: Birds are mentioned only because they are usually listed together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that birds teach nothing new. Since the משנה listed בהמה and חיה, it also mentioned עופות, as the three are usually grouped together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it taught domestic and wild animals, it also taught birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word עופות is not teaching a new law. It is there only because it naturally goes with the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an 'אגב' answer: a word is included only because it goes along with the others. Unlike בהמה and חיה, birds do not have their own reason to be listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because it already (an 'along the way' answer)

phrases.english: Since it taught domestic and wild animals,
it also taught birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עופות add no new law. They were listed only because they go together with בהמה and חיה.

steps.title: Isn't selling to a non-Jew obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and he may sell it to a גוי' and objects that this is obvious. If one may eat and benefit from the חמץ at that time, of course one may sell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he may sell it to a non-Jew.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה. It complains that this phrase seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already allows eating חמץ and feeding it to animals during this time. Selling it seems no different, so why say it? The גמרא assumes every phrase in a משנה teaches something.

keyTerms.meaning: And he may sell it to a non-Jew

phrases.english: 'And he may sell it to a non-Jew.'
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating and benefiting from חמץ are allowed at this time, selling it is obviously allowed, so the phrase seems unneeded.

steps.title: The phrase rejects the view of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the phrase is needed to exclude the opinion of בית שמאי in a ברייתא. They say a person may not sell his חמץ to a גוי unless he knows it will be finished before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of this תנא, as it was taught: בית שמאי say a person may not sell his חמץ to a non-Jew unless he knows it will be used up before פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the phrase is not obvious after all. There is a תנא who disagrees, and the משנה is rejecting that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that a Jew is still connected to his חמץ even after selling it. If the גוי still has it on פסח, that is a problem. So for them, selling is not obvious at all, and the משנה's words teach that we do not follow this view.

keyTerms.meaning: That it will be used up

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי do not say the חמץ is forbidden to sell at this time in general. They allow it only if he knows it will be finished before פסח.

phrases.english: To exclude this תנא, as it was taught:
בית שמאי say:
A person may not sell his חמץ to a non-Jew
unless he knows about it
that it will be used up before פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the phrase is needed to reject a disputing opinion (לאפוקי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the phrase, we might follow בית שמאי and require that the חמץ be finished before פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling to a גוי is allowed without that condition, against בית שמאי.

steps.title: בית הלל: whenever eating is allowed, selling is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the view of בית הלל. For the whole time one may eat חמץ, one may also sell it. This is the view the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: whenever it is permitted to eat, it is permitted to sell.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side of the argument. בית הלל's rule matches the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית הלל, once the חמץ is sold, the Jew is no longer responsible for it. So the only question is whether he may still use it now. The משנה's phrase 'כל שעה שמותר לאכול' echoes בית הלל's exact language.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows בית הלל. As long as one may eat חמץ, one may sell it to a גוי, even if the גוי will still have it on פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the idea that after a sale, the חמץ is no longer the Jew's responsibility. It underlies the later practice of selling חמץ before פסח.

phrases.english: And בית הלל say:
The whole time that it is permitted to eat,
it is permitted to sell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 23 by giving the view the משנה adopts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whenever one may eat חמץ, one may sell it to a גוי, with no need for it to be finished before פסח.
